questions.def: "Managed to" expresses ability in a specific past situation.
questions.question: Despite his injury, he ___ finish the race.

questions.def: "Became able to" describes acquired ability in the past.
questions.question: She ___ speak French fluently after living in Paris.

questions.def: "Can" doesn't need "to" before the verb.
questions.question: I can to swim across the lake when I was younger.

questions.def: "Enables" means allows or makes possible in the present.
questions.question: The new software ___ us to work more efficiently.

questions.def: "Has been able to" describes ability over a period of time.
questions.question: He ___ play the piano since he was five.

questions.def: "Were capable of" shows a general ability in the past.
questions.question: They ___ fix the car themselves, which saved money.

questions.def: Use "can" or "is able to" to express ability.
questions.question: She is being able to solve complex problems quickly.

questions.def: "Empowered" means gave ability or authority in the past.
questions.question: The training ___ the employees to handle difficult situations.

questions.def: "Could" expresses a wish about a present ability.
questions.question: I wish I ___ fly.

questions.def: "Could have" expresses a past possibility or ability.
questions.question: If I had studied harder, I ___ passed the exam.

questions.def: The adjective must come before "enough": "skilled enough".
questions.question: Being enough skilled, she managed to complete the project.

questions.def: "Skill" is the noun form, referring to the ability itself.
questions.question: Her ___ in negotiation is highly valued.

questions.def: "Could" describes general past ability.
questions.question: By the time he was ten, he ___ already speak three languages.

questions.def: Complex phrase for almost having an ability.
questions.correct: was on the verge of being able to
options: was on the verge of being able to
questions.question: The athlete ___ break the world record.

questions.def: "Potential" refers to a future ability.
questions.question: The company sees his ___ to lead the team.

questions.def: "Was able" emphasizes successful effort to do something.
questions.question: She ___ to convince him, despite his initial reluctance.

questions.def: "Could have" suggests a missed opportunity or ability.
questions.question: They ___ have finished the project on time if they'd worked harder.

questions.def: "Competent" means having the necessary ability or skill.
questions.question: The team needs a ___ leader.

questions.def: "Couldn't help but" means unable to stop oneself.
questions.question: He ___ help but laugh when he heard the joke.

questions.def: "Became able" suggests acquired ability in the past.
questions.question: She ___ to understand the lecture after reading the textbook.

questions.def: Use "know how to" to express ability to do something.
questions.question: I am knowing how to solve this problem.

questions.def: "Skillful" is the adjective form of skill.
questions.question: She is a ___ negotiator.

questions.def: "Were unable to" describes a lack of ability in the past.
questions.question: They ___ reach the summit before nightfall.

questions.def: "Wasn't able" describes a specific instance of inability.
questions.question: I ___ to open the jar until I used a tool.

questions.def: Use "has the ability" to show general ability.
questions.question: He is having the ability to inspire others.

questions.def: "Mastered" means acquired complete skill in something.
questions.question: She ___ the art of negotiation.

questions.def: "Can't believe" expresses disbelief or surprise.
questions.question: I ___ believe how quickly he learned.

questions.def: "Became able to" shows a developed ability.
questions.question: She ___ run a marathon by training hard.

questions.def: "Able to" expresses specific ability in a past situation.
questions.question: Despite the injury, he was ___ to finish the marathon.

questions.def: "Was able to" expresses a specific past ability, not a general one.
questions.question: She ___ speak French fluently after living in Paris.
